questions.stem_text: Anscombe criticizes Sidgwick on the grounds that:

options.A: he supports the principle of consequentialism.
options.B: he endorses the divine law conception of ethics.
options.C: he claims that there is a "natural balance" to the universe.
options.D: he does not believe in the principle of double effect.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - he supports the principle of consequentialism.

questions.stem_text:
If it were known that a policy would wipe out several animal species without negatively
affecting human beings, Baxter would most likely say that

options.A: this policy is morally problematic because it disrupts the natural order.
options.B: this policy is morally problematic because it negatively impacts biodiversity.
options.C: this policy is morally acceptable because it does not harm human beings.
options.E: this policy is morally obligatory because it prioritizes human beings.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - this policy is morally unproblematic.

questions.stem_text: According to Stevenson, moral disagreements involve:
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: E - disagreement in interest.
